knowledge_point.title: Calculating Indefinite Integrals Using Substitution with Inverse Tangent

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{4}{252 x^{2} + 7}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
252 x^{2} + 7=7(1+(36)x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=6 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=6,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{6})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{4}{252 x^{2} + 7}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{7}\int \frac{1}{1+(6 x)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{7}(\frac{1}{6})\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2}{21}\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}}{21}+C \\  &= \frac{2 \operatorname{arctan}{\left(6 x \right)}}{21}+C\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{4}{2 x^{2} + 49}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
2 x^{2} + 49=49(1+(\frac{2}{49})x^{2})
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{7}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{7},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{7 \sqrt{2}}{2})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{4}{2 x^{2} + 49}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{49}\int \frac{1}{1+(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{7})^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{49}(\frac{7 \sqrt{2}}{2})\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{2}}{7}\int \frac{1}{1+u^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{2} \operatorname{arctan}{\left(u \right)}}{7}+C \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{2} \operatorname{arctan}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{7} \right)}}{7}+C\end{aligned}
$$
